RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 30

Panel composition alone proves nothing. Women are a majority in education; an all-female panel is unremarkable and raising it reads as an insinuation you can't support — it shifts attention from your strong argument to your weakest one.

Your strong argument is the qualifications comparison: a master's in educational leadership plus five years as deputy principal against "courses" and no documented leadership experience. In most Nordic/EU frameworks, if a candidate of the other sex with weaker formal qualifications is appointed, the employer must justify it — and they owe you written reasons, which they've ignored for two weeks.

So: send a formal written reminder citing your right to reasons. Judge the decision after you see their stated criteria. Then reassess.
